column1: # SCHEMAS.tsv -- the mapping document: each first-tier application's fields, mapped onto the lens.
# This file IS the "map" frame (their runtime): anyone can apply it by hand or in any language.
# bin/ep1mo is the "transformer" frame (our runtime) and reads its rules from here, never from code.
# app: pmo.todos | pmo.projects | tavern.task | kiosk.stack | epmo.export (EPMO Convention v0.1).
# rule:  a=b;c=d   value map onto the lens dim (left = the app's value, right = a LENS.tsv value)
#        placement  take the dim from r/epmo/PLACEMENTS.tsv by the row's project key
#        quote      carried verbatim as the first of the three layers (the quote layer)
#        key        the row's identity in its own app; carried, never reinterpreted
#        provenance a signature, chain or receipt: carried so the row can be checked at its source
# loss: what the arrow drops, said in words. "none" is a claim ep1mo roundtrip tests.
# Sources: pmo/bin/pmo-lib.sh and doc/LEDGER-SPEC.md; tavern.py 2.3.1 (Room.tasks, task_priority, DUE_TAG);

column6: the order the id implies was never negotiated (facts/pmo-is-two-compatibility-layers-below-the-heuristic.md)
DONE and DOING both read as bet; a word outside the three reads as guess and its spelling is lost
an unweighted rank; no cardinality, so it is carried, not mapped
a tag that is a proper gap (tx1lk) carries no meaning yet
maintenance and active both read as bet
the path itself is carried as key, not interpreted
claimed and closed both read as bet
the date is carried as key; any due date marks the row forecast too
a room's membership is not in the task, so every room reads as team
who claimed is carried as key
the layer's name is carried as key
open is a held tension, not a guess; the distinction is kept in key
HOLD covers every unknown state word upstream
Tavern tasks carry no project; the export assigns one (judged), and a wrong key places the row wrongly
